card.name: Casual hedging idioms in informal prose
card.fires_on: Words inside casual, chatty English phrases that soften or dismiss a point, such as "none too keen", "no big deal", "never mind that", "don't worry". Mostly informal blog-style text.

modes.label: Understatement idioms
modes.description: Words within phrases like "none too keen" or "no big deal" that play something down.
modes.example: Mr. Lawrence was none<< too>> keen on their additions

modes.label: Reassuring asides
modes.description: Words in parenthetical or dismissive asides addressed to the reader, like "don't worry" or "never mind that".
modes.example: But never mind<< that>> for now.

card.writes: It leans the output away from words about convenience and toward Chinese words of sacrifice, miracle and "called", so the effect is unclear.
card.plain: It lights up on relaxed, chatty phrases where the writer plays something down or reassures the reader.
